A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Sparse Feature Circuits and SHIFT. Their main texts and complete appendices, including equations, tables and circuit diagrams, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia-70M circuit evaluations, Bias in Bios classifier experiments, SAE evaluations, human interpretability ratings and automatically discovered circuit analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original Pythia experiments and human ratings and adds original Gemma-2-2B circuit and classifier experiments, including new ablation results.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the stated Jacobian-subtraction procedure for computing direct edge effects with stop-gradients at intermediate nodes. The Gemma application also excludes BOS features from SHIFT ablation (Appendix B.2). These are limited procedural adaptations within the retained circuit-discovery and SHIFT framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four subject-verb agreement tasks, the same Bias in Bios profession/gender setting, and The Pile for SAE training and behavior discovery. Adding Gemma changes model configurations rather than represented datasets, populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds a random-feature ablation comparator to the classifier experiment and Table 2. CBP, feature and neuron skylines, the original classifier and the oracle remain. SHIFT with neurons is abandoned without quantitative results in both versions.

E3.justification: v3 adds Gemma-2-2B and Gemma Scope configurations for agreement and classification experiments. Its Gemma probe uses layer 22, selected using balanced data to obtain poor initial generalization; BOS features are excluded from SHIFT and the feature skyline. Case-study selection now targets faithfulness above 0.2. The reported Pythia SAE buffer also changes from 10,000 tokens to 10,000 contexts, without establishing that training was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds matched-count random-feature ablations to test the importance of informed feature selection. Figure 3 extends circuit-complement and SAE-error ablation analyses to Gemma. Appendix C adds four Gemma agreement-circuit case studies and an NP number-tracking feature example, substantially expanding the mechanistic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance procedures for these experiments. Human-rating means retain the same reporting practice. The faint Figure 3 curves represent syntactic structures, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds Gemma results throughout Figures 3–4 and Table 2; Gemma SHIFT plus retraining achieves 95.0% profession and 92.9% worst-group accuracy. Pythia Table 2 revisions include CBP profession accuracy 82.5 to 83.3, neuron-skyline profession accuracy 80.6 to 75.5, and feature-skyline gender accuracy 54.0 to 54.3; Pythia SHIFT scores remain unchanged. The reported Pythia relative-clause circuit changes from 69 nodes and 0.19 faithfulness to 86 nodes and 0.21, under the revised case-study selection description.

T1.justification: Equation 4 adds the missing 1/N normalization to the integrated-gradients approximation. Appendix B inserts ReLU into the previously affine SAE encoder formula, consistent with v3's nonnegative feature definition. These are localized corrections to the mathematical specification; no new theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three central contributions: scalable sparse feature circuit discovery, SHIFT without disambiguating labeled data, and an unsupervised pipeline discovering thousands of behavior circuits. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets Gemma's agreement mechanism through NP number trackers and explains neuron-ablation failure through shared usefulness for gender and profession prediction. It discusses influential but uninterpretable BOS features and qualifies feature labeling as task- and annotator-dependent. The earlier suggestion that error-node attribution could measure SAE quality is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 documents Gemma SAE width, attachment locations, selection by L0 closest to 100, and BOS-feature handling. Appendix E.1 specifies Gemma probe-layer selection, while the text identifies Neuronpedia for feature inspection. These extend existing implementation documentation; the previously disclosed code, data, SAE and circuit releases remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds recent SAE and interpretability references, including Gao et al. (2024), Templeton et al. (2024), Rajamanoharan et al. (2024a,b), Gemma Scope, Neuronpedia, Hanna et al. (2024) and Mueller et al. (2024). This updates the research context and public-resource positioning while retaining the central comparisons with hypothesis-driven interpretation and methods requiring disambiguating data.

P1.justification: The formulation and clustering explanations are expanded, classifier-training documentation is rewritten, and a dedicated Reproducibility section is added. Most appendices are reorganized: circuit galleries and sample features move earlier, human ratings move later, and the linear-approximation analysis moves to the end. This substantially changes the document's explanatory organization.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands to a two-model, four-panel display; Figure 4 gains a Gemma circuit summary; and Table 2 gains model-specific column groups and a random-ablation row. Four Gemma circuit diagrams and an NP-tracker example are added, existing circuit displays gain layer/token labels, and v1's edge-computation schematic is removed. Other displays are relocated within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation previously confined to Pythia-70M: Gemma-2-2B experiments, annotated circuits and random-ablation controls provide evidence for broader applicability and the importance of informed feature selection (Figures 3–4, Table 2, Appendix C). Formula corrections and model-specific documentation improve technical clarity. Gemma's deliberately poorly generalizing probe is selected using balanced data (Appendix E.1), limiting that demonstration, and uncertainty reporting remains absent. These limitations temper but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in supporting evidence.
